findings.text: Early code-patching service writes a byte sequence to kernel or module text. Module text already marked non-executable is updated directly, while other targets are updated with interrupts suppressed and a serializing step after the copy.

Relocation need is decided by whether a referenced target falls outside the replacement block. In-block references are left alone, while outside references receive a delta adjustment guarded by a signed-range check.

Direct-call substitution requires a short call replacement shape and a longer indirect call source shape. Mismatched shapes abort, a missing target falls back to a bug handler, and a no-operation target suppresses emission.
Patch sites normalize runs of no-operation instructions before writing text. Scanning decodes forward, coalesces adjacent no-operation encodings, and rewrites each run with a preferred padding form.
Early patching suppresses local interrupts around the non-module update path and restores them afterwards, so the copy plus serialization appears atomic to local interrupt handlers.

Demand fault on the vdso area resolves the fault offset against the process image size. In-range offsets return the corresponding image page with a reference held, while missing images or out-of-range offsets report a bus error.

Moving the vdso preserves execution continuity for a thread currently inside the old range. The saved instruction pointer offset is re-based onto the new base and the cached process base pointer is refreshed.
Vdso installation holds the address-space write lock while reserving and installing adjacent mappings. Failures unwind already installed parts before releasing the lock and returning an error.
A process may hold at most one vdso family installation. A full scan rejects a second install when any vdso, variable-data, or variable-clock special mapping already exists.

Process creation installs the appropriate vdso image based on build mode, compatibility mode, and enable controls. The 64-bit, 32-bit, and extended 32-bit images each have a dedicated selection path with a disabled fast return.

Vdso sigreturn detection checks that the current image is the 32-bit vdso and that the saved instruction pointer matches one of two landing offsets. Other images or positions are not treated as vdso returns.

Two special-mapping descriptors associate vdso and variable-clock areas with their fault handlers, with the vdso descriptor also carrying a move handler. Distinct names identify the areas for diagnostics.

Vsyscall behavior follows a boot-selected mode of emulate, execute-only, or none. The mode controls whether a backing page is installed, whether gate metadata is exposed, and whether faults are emulated or rejected.

Page-fault and protection-fault helpers decide whether a faulting address should enter vsyscall emulation. Checks include user-mode fault attributes, instruction-fetch versus data-access distinction, and recognition of the fixed vsyscall address range.

Failed emulation paths warn at a rate-limited level and terminate the access with a fault signal. Bad stacks, misaligned addresses, unwritable user buffers, and seccomp interference all lead to signals rather than silent continuation.

The vsyscall gate is described as a single fixed page with read and execute attributes plus a diagnostic name operation. Visibility depends on mode and, for compatibility processes, on a per-process gate flag; a lock-free helper tests the fixed page without process context.

Clearing one CPU capability transitively clears all capabilities that depend on it until no further change occurs. Boot-wide clears update global state and a cleared mask, while per-CPU clears update only the given descriptor.
Accessor returns the cached virtual address of the boot-CPU paravirtual clock time information block for use by variable-clock fault handling.

Corrected-error firmware-first enablement records the firmware threshold, requires a firmware-first flag and a non-zero bank count, announces enablement, and disables each listed machine-check bank. Memory-error reports are forwarded to the machine-check handler when enabled.

User-visible names identify the vdso area, the variable-clock area, the vsyscall gate, and the vsyscall trace system with its include location. These labels are stable interfaces for tools and mappings.
Variable-clock faults serve only defined clock offsets and only when the corresponding clock mode was previously used and a backing page exists. Other offsets or unused modes report a bus error.

Early vsyscall initialization marks each paging level covering the fixed address as user accessible when emulation is selected, and verifies that the fixed mapping address matches the expected constant.
Requests to disable an out-of-range machine-check bank emit a firmware-bug warning and return without broadcasting. Valid banks are recorded as disabled and then disabled on every CPU.

Vdso relocation and installation refresh the recorded ranges of vdso critical sections used by robust futex list handling, with separate 64-bit and 32-bit ranges. A configuration without that support uses an empty update operation.
